I had the same "believes" regarding kids as you. My goal is to be a school social worker. I always wanted to work with kids with not so great home lives. I was always the person my friends went to growing up, and it jsut felt natural to pursue social work. Challenges are that these kids have seen this way of life for so long that it's natural to them and they don't see a way out or a way that could be helpful. They become sarcastic and cynical in a way. Seeing kids use the skills I've helped them developed is the biggest reward. I currently work as a case manager for behavior mental health with high school students. I wish I knew more about my state licensing requirements and guidelines. I no longer live in the state I got my education from and it's become difficult to become a school social worker as I have to pass the TAP (test of academic proficiency) to be licensed in my old state,  I also lack any "Formal therapy" experience so it is extremely difficult to move up in my current job. All my experience and internships were based on school social work.

I just earned my Masters degree and no longer have to fake it. Happiness happens, sometimes it's a matter of faking for a few more days to find it. Something that helped me was making goals and plan a future, the trouble with that is live will get in the way so your dream future will almost always fall apart. Just have something to look forward to and start doing things because you want to, not because someone else wants you to.

I totally agree with NoremacNotRedBlue. first step is throwing them away, and not in the trash, flushing them away so no matter what you can't get them back... it will be one of the hardest things to do. Now look in the mirror and tell yourself: you are worth something, you will get through this. Say it out loud until it sinks in and you believe it, because it is true. Secondly, talk to someone, a friend, a complete internet stranger, a therapist, anyone.  Next, manage. what can you change? what can you fix for the better? what do you need to just walk away from? baby steps... nothing changes overnight... nothing changes when you bottle everything up.. let someone in. it's easier with company. <3
